messages.content:
Outcome: Depressive symptoms (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: no effect
Claim: Vitamin D3 supplementation did not lower depression scores compared with placebo in healthy women over winter.
Sentence: "We found no evidence of lower depression (P = 0·339), lower anxiety (P = 0·862), higher flourishing (P = 0·453), higher positive moods (P = 0·518) or lower negative moods (P = 0·538) in the treatment group compared with the control group at follow-up."
Measured as: depression (Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale)
Population: 152 healthy women aged 18-40 years in Dunedin, New Zealand
Intervention: 50 000 IU oral vitamin D3 once per month for 6 months
Comparator: placebo
Design: randomized controlled trial
Sample size: 152
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: benefit
Claim: In adults with MDD, higher serum 25(OH)D levels were inversely associated with depression severity (HDRS scores) in adjusted models.
Sentence: "In adjusted models, higher serum 25(OH)D levels remained inversely associated with HDRS scores, SIS scores, and total SPS scores."
Measured as: depressive symptom severity (HDRS)
Population: 97 adults aged 18-65 years diagnosed with MDD per DSM-5
Intervention: Serum 25(OH)D level (measured, not administered)
Comparator: Lower versus higher serum 25(OH)D levels across participants
Design: cross-sectional study
Sample size: 97
baseline_vitamin_d_status: below_20_ng_ml
